extracted.intended_audience: educated early-18th-century readers of The Spectator; general public interested in morals, manners, church practice, and rhetoric
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of prescriptive principles and evaluative criteria embedded in Spectator essays and letters on topics such as petitions for office, church music and decorum, personal cleanliness, and oratory. The page is a collection of short moralising pieces and correspondent letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recompense based on genuine meritorious suffering
rubrics_metrics.description: When [sufferings] are such as have promoted a good Cause, and fallen upon a Man undeservedly, they have a Right to be heard and recompensed beyond any other Pretensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims for offices or rewards should rest on undeserved injuries suffered in service of a good cause. Such genuine sacrifices justify preferential consideration. (Contrast with later entries showing abusive/absurd petitions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Party-sufferings from rashness or indiscretion do not merit reward
rubrics_metrics.description: But when they rise out of Rashness or Indiscretion, and the Pursuit of such Measures as have rather ruined, than promoted the Interest they aim at... they only serve to recommend them to the Children of Violence or Folly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a person's hardships are the result of their own imprudence or the pursuit of counterproductive measures, those 'sufferings' should not be treated as grounds for patronage or office. Use this to distinguish deserving from undeserving claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurd petition examples as anti-patterns for entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of ridiculous pretensions to preferment: petitions for reward because one roasted an ox on the king's birth-day, drank the prince's health in bad times, cursed an opponent publicly, let a beard grow during the interregnum, or carried an important letter with alleged decisive influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete examples illustrate what does not count as legitimate merit: convivial excesses, petty personal grievances, bawdy or violent behaviour, or mere proximity to events. They are warnings against accepting trivial or comic claims as grounds for appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical worship as solemn preparation for receiving divine truths
rubrics_metrics.description: There is something very laudable in the Custom of a Voluntary before the first Lesson; by this we are supposed to be prepared for the Admission of those Divine Truths, which we are shortly to receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modest musical preludes (voluntaries) to calm the mind and prepare congregants for scripture and sermon; music should serve a devotional, preparatory function rather than merely entertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer modesty in church music over pompous foreign styles
rubrics_metrics.description: I am swayed by my Judgment to the Modesty which is observed in the musical Part of our Devotions. Methinks there is something very laudable in the Custom ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The writer recommends the restrained English style of church music as better suited to devotion than ostentatious continental pomp which 'most affects our Senses' but may not better the soul.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthems and sacred music relieve spiritual languor and raise devotion
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Spirits begin to languish ... she takes care to allow them a pious Respite, and relieves them with the Raptures of an Anthem. Nor can we doubt that the sublimest Poetry, softened in the most moving Strains of Musick, can ever fail of humbling or exalting the Soul to any Pitch of Devotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ anthems and moving sacred music strategically to renew attention and to heighten emotional receptivity to devotion; music paired with sublime poetry can humble and exalt the soul.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music should express and reinforce the meaning of sacred texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Who can hear the Terrors of the Lord of Hosts described in the most expressive Melody, without being awed into a Veneration? or who can hear the kind and endearing Attributes of a merciful Father, and not be softened into Love towards him!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select musical settings that reflect and intensify the affective content of the text (awe for divine terrors; tenderness for mercy), so the music reinforces the sermon/scripture rather than distracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church decorum: oppose 'rattling clubs'—no mockery or noisy signalling
rubrics_metrics.description: These gay Fellows... set up for Criticks without any Tincture of Letters ... If any Sentiments are delivered too Sublime ... they are all immediately upon their Watch, fixing their Eyes upon each other ... with odd Looks and Gesticulations confer together in so loud and clamorous a manner ... and aiming to propagate their Noise through all the Church, by Signals given to the adjoyning Seats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage congregational factions that mock or disrupt sermons. Avoid coordinated signals, loud gestures, or side-conferences that prevent others from hearing and that transform the pew into a club rather than a place of worship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter in sacred transactions is highly improper
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter, where things Sacred are transacted, is far less pardonable than Whining at a Conventicle; the last has at least a Semblance of Grace... but the first has no Excuse, breaking through all the Rules of Order and Decency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from laughter and levity during worship services; such behaviour shows remissness of mind and disrespect to the sanctity of the place and the minister.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veneration for the sanctity of place and respect for the minister
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall not here enter upon the Veneration due to the Sanctity of the Place, the Reverence owing to the Minister, or the Respect that so great an Assembly as a whole Parish may justly claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe respectful behaviour in houses of worship: silence, attention, and decorum are due both to the sacred space and to the person delivering the sermon; actions contrary to this violate laws and decency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleanliness is a fundamental mark of politeness
rubrics_metrics.description: It is universally agreed upon, that no one, unadorn'd with this Virtue, can go into Company without giving a manifest Offence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal cleanliness is a social duty; entering company without cleanliness offends. The obligation rises with social status: the more elevated the fortune, the more incumbent the duty of appearing clean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleanliness fosters and preserves love and attractiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Cleanliness may be said to be the Foster-Mother of Love. Beauty indeed most commonly produces that Passion in the Mind, but Cleanliness preserves it. An indifferent Face and Person, kept in perpetual Neatness, had won many a Heart from a pretty Slattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain neatness to conserve affection and personal appeal; outward orderliness contributes strongly to perceived attractiveness, even compensating for lesser natural beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleanliness bears analogy to purity of mind
rubrics_metrics.description: It bears a great Analogy with Purity of Mind, and naturally inspires refined Sentiments and Passions... pure and unsullied Thoughts are naturally suggested to the Mind, by those Objects that perpetually encompass us, when they are beautiful and elegant in their kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate outward cleanliness and elegant surroundings as a means of encouraging inward purity of thought and sentiment; habitual exposure to neatness inclines the mind toward refinement and away from vice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleanliness promotes health and discourages vices
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an excellent Preservative of Health; and that several Vices, destructive both to Mind and Body, are inconsistent with the Habit of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame cleanliness as practical moral and physical hygiene: regular cleanliness supports bodily health and is incompatible with many vices, thus serving both private and public goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use elevated, eternal topics to strengthen oratory's persuasive power
rubrics_metrics.description: Christianity... as it brings the Consideration of another Life into the Question, as it proposes Rewards and Punishments of a higher Nature, and a longer Continuance, is more adapted to affect the Minds of the Audience... so much are the Motives to Persuasion under Christianity greater than those which meer moral Considerations could supply us with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose subjects that concern eternal stakes (immortality, judgment, resurrection) to produce stronger emotional and moral persuasion; such topics enlarge an audience's motives and make rhetoric more effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Marvellous/sublime is the master-piece of eloquence
rubrics_metrics.description: There is another Part of Eloquence, which is indeed its Master-piece; I mean the Marvellous or Sublime. In this the Christian Orator has the Advantage beyond Contradiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for the sublime—great, elevated conceptions and imagery—in oratory. Cultivating a sense of the marvellous (through revelation or grand themes) provides material for the highest form of rhetorical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study great and heavenly matters to expand the orator's imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Tully requires in his Perfect Orator some Skill in the Nature of Heavenly Bodies, because, says he, his Mind will become more extensive and unconfined... the Study of those great and glorious Mysteries which Revelation has discovered to us... the noblest Parts of this System of the World are as much inferiour, as the Creature is less excellent than its Creator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden intellectual horizons by studying cosmology, revelation, and lofty mysteries; such studies free and enlarge the mind, enabling more exalted and expansive rhetoric when returning to human subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance (doctrine) can exceed form in lasting eloquence—St Paul as model
rubrics_metrics.description: The Power of the Doctrines he delivered... have still the Power, when preached by a skilful Orator, to make us break out in the same Expressions... That no one Orator has left us so visible Marks and Footsteps of his Eloquence as our Apostle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the intrinsic power of ideas and doctrines can produce enduring eloquence beyond merely rhetorical skill. Use substantial, morally weighty content as the core of persuasive speech—St Paul is given as exemplar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt style to legal and contextual constraints of the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: It may perhaps be wondered at, that in his Reasonings upon Idolatry at Athens... he confines himself to strict Argument only; but... That all Attempts upon the Affections and Strokes of Oratory were expressly forbidden, by the Laws of that Country, in Courts of Judicature. His want of Eloquence therefore here, was the Effect of his exact Conformity to the Laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor rhetorical approach to institutional and legal boundaries: where appeals to emotion are forbidden or inappropriate, rely on strict argument; adapt to audience expectations and regulatory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical example: clergy may look to St Paul as a model for improving sermons
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sum of all this Discourse is, That our Clergy have no farther to look for an Example of the Perfection they may arrive at, than to St. Paul's Harangues; that when he... was heard, admired, and made a Standard to succeeding Ages... our Clergy may learn, That... St. Paul has given them a noble Example of, and the Christian Religion has furnished them with certain Means of attaining to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clergy seeking to elevate sermon quality should study St Paul's mode of addressing doctrine and affect, using Christian revelation as source material to aspire to greater eloquence and persuasive force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrinal content combined with skilful delivery yields greatest effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The latter Part of [Longinus'] Judgment adds great Weight to his Opinion of St. Paul's Abilities, since, under all the Prejudice of Opinions directly opposite, he is constrained to acknowledge the Merit of that Apostle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue both substantial doctrinal/material content and competent rhetorical delivery. Great content can compel admiration even from critics; but the combination of material and skill is decisive.
